access_used: public sample in paper/repo/card only (full data needs the Nymeria CC BY-NC click-through / AEA and ADT license acceptance with email)
note: Nymeria narration CSVs come only after the email-and-accept download form (the nymeria_dataset repo's NarrationLoader is still a stub), so example 1 is the paper's own Figure 6 example of the three description levels (no timestamps, no clip id). Example 2 is the real AEA speech.csv shipped as unit-test data in the Apache-2.0 projectaria_tools repo: one row per ASR word with device-clock start/end in nanoseconds (converted to seconds in the timeline) and a confidence. ADT has no language annotations. No clip (AEA license forbids redistribution).

examples.title: Nymeria: three annotation levels (motion narration, atomic action, 30-s summary) — paper Figure 6
examples.raw: Figure 6 : Hierarchical narration example. (left) motion narration of 5s clip – “C straightens the body to receive a badminton racket from his peer. C extends the right arms towards the bat, with the left arm slightly bent. C takes a step forward with the left foot. C focuses on the racket.” (middle) Atomic action of 5s clip – “C lifts the right leg to kick a soccer ball in front of a building.” (right) Activity summarization of 30s clip – “C bikes on the road with a peer.”
